text:
Carol will likely win. The "as is" clause disclaims only implied warranties, while the ad's "1964 Thunderbird" and the website photo are express statements of fact that formed part of the basis of the bargain, so the wrong model year is a breach even without seller fault, and the parol evidence rule does not bar them because they also support fraud. Her likely remedy is damages equal to the difference between the 1964 and 1968 values, or rescission. The team note saying the buyer must prove carelessness is wrong for express warranty liability; fault matters mainly for fraud and punitive damages.

CONFIDENCE: 72
